items.titleEn: Gold price trades near $4,050/oz after preliminary Consumer Sentiment rises to 51, inflation expectations ease
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market is coming off its post-payrolls lows after the latest data showed consumer sentiment in the U.S. improving beyond expectations, while inflation expectations ticked lower. The University of Michigan announced on Friday that the preliminary reading of its Consumer Sentiment survey for November was 51. The data was better than expectations, as the consensus forecast of economists called for a reading of 48, the same as October’s final reading. “Consumer sentiment ticked up about 6% in the preliminary read,” said Surveys of Consumers Director Joanne Hsu in the report. “Modest improvements in multiple domains, including expected personal finances and business conditions, were concentrated primarily among independents. While sentiment lifted for lower- and middle-wealth consumers, it fell 5% for those with the largest stock portfolios in the wake of a relatively turbulent period in stock markets.”

Gold falls as U.S. payrolls surge by 165,000, strengthening December Fed hike case - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold prices were lower and spot silver prices were modestly higher in early U.S. trading Friday, as investors assessed the latest U.S. employment figures following Thursday's sharp equity-market selloff and renewed tensions involving Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. economy added substantially more jobs than expected in October, reinforcing the case for another Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December and driving Treasury yields and the dollar higher immediately after the release. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,050.95 an ounce, down $34.10, or 0.89%, while spot silver was trading near $51.864, up $0.089, or 0.17%. The U.S. Labor Department reported Friday that nonfarm payroll employment increased by 165,000 in October, substantially exceeding economists' expectations for approximately 65,000 new jobs and accelerating from an upwardly revised September gain of 60,000. The unemployment rate declined to 4.1% from 4.2%, while average hourly earnings increased 0.4% on the month, above expectations for a 0.3% gain. Average hourly earnings were 3.1% higher than a year earlier. The stronger employment and wage figures indicated that labor-market conditions remain resilient despite elevated borrowing costs, geopolitical uncertainty and recent weakness in technology shares. Revisions provided additional evidence of improving employment conditions. August payroll growth was revised higher by 53,000 to 186,000, while September's increase was revised upward by 31,000 to 60,000. The two-month revisions added a combined 84,000 jobs to previously reported employment. Professional and business services led October hiring with 70,000 additional positions, followed by health care with 42,000 and transportation and warehousing with 25,000. Manufacturing employment increased by 19,000. The labor-force participation rate held at 61.9%, while the average workweek remained unchanged at 34.4 hours. The report suggests that demand for labor remains stronger than anticipated, although hiring continues to vary considerably across industries.

gold prices see some selling pressure as US economy created 165k in October
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - After a slow summer, the U.S. labor market appears to be picking up significant momentum, which, as expected, is once again putting pressure on gold, with renewed focus on support at $4,000 an ounce. U.S. nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000 last month, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The monthly figure significantly beat consensus forecasts, as economists had expected job gains of around 60,000. At the same time, the unemployment rate dropped to 4.1%. Economists had expected the rate to remain unchanged at 4.2%.
